taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Bidens laevis (L.) Britton, Sterns & Poggenb. Source pool iNaturalist taxon 75766.
look_here_first: Start with a middle stem leaf: B. laevis has SIMPLE, usually sessile leaves, unlike the 3–5 leaflets of B. frondosa. Then examine the conspicuous radiate heads (usually 7–8 rays, 10–25 mm) and mature cypselae to separate it from B. cernua.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved Master Plant Pool row 135 (My iNaturalist Flora and Hays County native pool); taxonomy and diagnostic review dated 2026-10-08
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO supports Texas nativity at state level; Hays source flag alone does not satisfy the three-target-county PASS rule.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial wetland or shoreline herb, often in shallow water or damp soils.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, simple and usually sessile stem leaves; toothed margins.
morphology_keys.heads: Conspicuous yellow ray florets, usually 7–8, commonly 10–25 mm long (FNA); central disk florets numerous.
morphology_keys.fruits: Outer cypselae approximately 6–8 mm; inner cypselae approximately 8–10 mm (FNA); confirm with scale and awn details.
best_field_traits: mature cypselae of two length classes

comparisons.key_distinctions: B. frondosa typically has 3–5 leaflets and few or no rays; B. laevis has simple sessile leaves and conspicuous rays. B. cernua can also have simple leaves and showy rays in wetlands, so check bractlets, leaf base, and mature cypselae; do not use flower color or habitat alone. B. aristosa can be showy; verify leaf division and bractlets.
